To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the teacher and children together created a playful classroom by engaging in on going improvised activity.

The teachers and children in the classrooms studied collectively created a playful and improvised classroom environment by engaging with one another, the space, and the materials available at the moment in a playful and improvised manner.

1) the teachers and children in our two classrooms collectively created a playful environment by engaging in improvised activity; 2) the teachers served as skilled improviser, by creating new performances out of what was available at the time; 3) the teachers’ improvisational skills were developed through a combination of formal and informal training; and 4) improvisational theatre training may be a potentially useful form of teacher education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the teacher in the improvisational classroom.
the question of what we should create today.
how the teacher's presence in a playful early childhood classroom can be conceptualized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
improvisational teaching is an important part of the early childhood classroom.
improvisational theatre is an effective and efficient method of teacher education, especially for those who will be working with young children.
this study found that the teacher's role in the creation of play was not to plan or direct play, but rather to participate in improvisational activity alongside the children in the classroom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
improvisational theatre can be an effective tool to support teachers in creating playful learning environments.
the teachers and the children together improvised play, and that this improvisation was supported by the teachers' improvisational skills.
we found that improvisation is a way of teaching, a way of learning and a way of living.
The main takeaway from our work is that
teachers should consider their role as improvisers, and should be encouraged to improvise with their children.
the early childhood classroom is a site of collective improvisation, and that early childhood teachers are skilled improvisers.

the teacher's role in a play-based classroom is to improvise, to make the most of what is available at the moment and to create a playful classroom environment together with the children. (author abstract)
